subject: Archaeology
subcategory: Lost Cities of the Ancient World
title: Why Cities Disappear
description: Learn Why Cities Disappear in one minute.

hook.text: Every lost city was once someone's home. They disappear for surprisingly few reasons — and we keep repeating them.

buildup.text: Drought killed Tiwanaku. Earthquakes sank Pavlopetri. Volcanic ash buried Akrotiri. Nature is the top destroyer.

discovery.text: War destroyed Palmyra and Hampi. Political collapse emptied Teotihuacan. Human violence ranks second.

twist.text: Some cities simply moved. Constantinople did not disappear — it became Istanbul. Cities evolve, they do not always die.

climax.text: Climate change now threatens modern coastal cities with the same fate as ancient ones — rising seas and shifting climates.

punchline.text: Lost cities are warnings written in stone. We rarely read them.

quiz.question: What is the most common cause of cities being lost to history?
options: Economic decline and loss of trade routes
Natural disasters like drought, earthquakes, and volcanic eruptions
Conquest by rival empires who demolished the structures
